issues.legal_issue: Dismissal for default of an application seeking to reopen a decree does not constitute a review that starts a fresh limitation period for execution.
material_facts: A judgment-debtor applied to reopen a preliminary mortgage decree, but the application was dismissed for default without the court considering whether the decree should be reopened.
The application to restore the reopening proceeding was also dismissed.
The decree-holder later applied to execute the final decree.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal for default was not a review of the decree under Article 182, clause 3, of the Limitation Act, 1908, and did not provide a fresh starting point for limitation; the execution application was time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 182, clause 3, of the Limitation Act, 1908, a fresh starting point requires that the court undertake to review the relevant decree or order and decide the review. Even assuming an application under section 36 of the Bengal Money-lenders Act could be treated as an application for review, dismissal for default without consideration of the merits is not a review. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: execution_application and reopening_proceeding and reopening_dismissed_for_default and court_did_not_consider_reopening_merits

predicates.execution_application: A decree-holder applied to execute a decree.
predicates.reopening_proceeding: A judgment-debtor applied to have a decree reopened.
predicates.reopening_dismissed_for_default: The court dismissed the application to reopen the decree because of default.
predicates.court_did_not_consider_reopening_merits: The court did not consider whether the decree should be reopened.

issues.definition: When a decree-holder seeks execution and a judgment-debtor's reopening application was dismissed for default without consideration of its merits, the reopening proceeding does not restart the limitation period for execution.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal concerning a collateral proceeding does not start a fresh limitation period for execution of a decree when the appeal is not from the decree or order sought to be executed.
material_facts: A final mortgage decree was passed, and no appeal was taken from that decree.
The judgment-debtor appealed the dismissal of an application to restore the proceeding seeking to reopen the preliminary decree.
That appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution.
The decree-holder applied to execute the final decree more than three years after it was passed.
issues.conclusion: The appeal from the order in the collateral proceeding did not provide a fresh starting point for limitation under Article 182, clause 2, of the Limitation Act, 1908; the execution application was time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Article 182, clause 2, of the Limitation Act, 1908, must be read with the article's description of applications for execution of a decree or order. An appeal starts a fresh limitation period only when it is connected directly or immediately with the decree or order sought to be executed; an appeal from an order in a collateral proceeding does not suffice. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.execution_application: A decree-holder applied to execute a decree.
predicates.appeal_from_collateral_proceeding: A party appealed an order made in a proceeding related to, but collateral to, the decree sought to be executed.
predicates.appeal_not_from_decree_sought_to_be_exec: The appeal was not from the decree or order for which execution was sought.

issues.definition: When execution is sought and the appeal was from a collateral proceeding rather than from the decree sought to be executed, the collateral appeal does not restart the execution limitation period.
